notes: The booklet images are very dark and small; exact stud positions are not recoverable, so each 'joined' edge records which part sits on which. Ports are assigned so that each named stud/anti-stud port is used once.

Where a catalogue part (e.g. base plates 303026, grey plates 4211404, 1x6 plates, 2x2 brick 300326, 1x2 brick 300426) has fewer named ports than the real piece has studs, extra joins use a null port instead of reusing a named one. A null port means 'some other stud of that piece'.
For new part types (300226 2x3 brick, 362226 1x3 brick, 235726 corner brick) I listed enough stud/anti-stud ports so each join gets its own port.

Piece identities for the new types (300526=1x1 brick, 362226=1x3 brick, 300226=2x3 brick, 235726=corner brick, 4200023=curved brick, 379426=jumper plate, 395701=antenna) are inferred from inventory pictures and counts; all counts match the inventory page.
Pieces are black/dark in the book (rendered dark green); the base/frame grey pieces are light grey. The 'Sears Tower' name is printed on a base plate/tile.
Step 5 placement of the 1x6 tile and two 306926 tiles, and exactly which jumper plates the first bricks sit on, are best guesses.

Steps 9-16 are the stepped upper tower; tiles are placed on pieces with free studs as best as can be judged, and the three 1x2 bricks in step 16 are stacked into a column carrying the two antennas on its top two studs (the second antenna uses a null port on the top brick).
Base plates b1 and b2 are only held together via the 1x6 plates over the seam (step 2), not directly.
